newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares slip as dealers await more falls.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares slip as dealers await more falls.

text.p: Singapore shares edged down a little further on Wednesday morning as investors stood on the sidelines in anticipation of further falls.
By 0230 GMT, the benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index was 4.36 points lower at 2,181.36.
Dealers said the index appeared to be heading for a chart target of 2,150 points and could slip to 2,125 before bouncing.
Total volume in the first 90 minutes was 38.9 million shares, but much of the activity was retail trading in recently listed, small local shares.
"Again, there's little demand from funds," said a dealer.

Construction firm Wee Poh Holdings was the most active share for the third straight day with more than 10 million shares changing hands as retail investors took profits from its spectacular gains earlier in the week.
At its debut on Monday, Wee Poh climbed 85 percent to a high of Singapore $0.835, from its public offer price of S$0.45.
The share was last at S$0.725, down four cents from Tuesday.
Singapore Press rose 10 cents to S$12.80 after news it would be part of a bid for a full Singapore telecommunications licence when the local industry is deregulated in 2000.
